instruction: Tab-Route Panel with Mouse Bites The file `/home/user/Desktop/A.kicad_pcb` is a small irregular PCB with an L-shaped outline using mixed straight (`gr_line`) and curved (`gr_arc`) edges on Edge.Cuts. You must panelize this board into a 3x2 array. Produce a panelized KiCad PCB file at `/home/user/Desktop/panel.kicad_pcb` containing: 1. 6 copies of board A arranged in a 3-column x 2-row grid, with approximately 8 mm spacing between copies. Preserve each copy's two test points, nets, five straight outline sections, and two curved outline sections, except for the 2 mm straight-edge openings required by tabs. 2. Exactly one 2 mm-wide material tab bridge at each of the 10 interfaces: 4 horizontal board-to-board interfaces, 3 vertical board-to-board interfaces, and 3 top-row-to-rail interfaces. The 2 mm width is measured along the joined straight board edge; the bridge spans the routing gap. Bound each bridge with Edge.Cuts and do NOT place or terminate a tab on a curved (`gr_arc`) edge. 3. Mouse-bite perforation through each tab: one centered row of exactly 4 non-plated through-holes (`np_thru_hole`), each with a 0.5 mm drill at 1 mm center-to-center pitch. The row runs along the bridge span and its center coincides with the bridge center. 4. One top breakaway rail strip with closed Edge.Cuts boundaries. Its topmost edge must be one horizontal Edge.Cuts line across the full panel width on the Y-min side. 5. Overall panel outline <= 180x120 mm. 6. Write `/home/user/Desktop/edgecuts.svg` using exactly: `kicad-cli pcb export svg --layers Edge.Cuts --exclude-drawing-sheet --page-size-mode 2 --drill-shape-opt 2 --black-and-white --mode-single --output /home/user/Desktop/edgecuts.svg /home/user/Desktop/panel.kicad_pcb`. 7. Write `/home/user/Desktop/panel.drl` using exactly: `kicad-cli pcb export drill --output /home/user/Desktop /home/user/Desktop/panel.kicad_pcb`. Write `/home/user/Desktop/panel.kicad_pcb`, `/home/user/Desktop/edgecuts.svg`, and `/home/user/Desktop/panel.drl`. [Software] Use KiCad 10.0.2; run `kicad` for the GUI or `kicad-cli` for scripting/headless use (use PATH or the full install path). Before starting the work, the installed KiCad tools are `/usr/bin/kicad-cli`, `/usr/bin/pcbnew`, and `/usr/bin/eeschema`; use the one that matches the board or schematic operation.
